classification.difficultyReason: Apply exact trigonometric values and quadrant signs to coordinates on circles with different radii.

content.prompt: When the radius of the circle is not 1, the coordinates of a point on the circumference are given by $(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)$. Find the coordinates of the point $P$ in each diagram in exact form.

spec.description: Unshaded circle with plain horizontal and vertical axes, a marked point P on the 60-degree ray, and an arrowhead beyond the circumference. The positive horizontal intercept is labelled 4.
spec.mathematics: Circle radius 4; P=(4 cos 60°,4 sin 60°). Diagram coordinates are normalised by the radius.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied radius, angle and point label are visible; coordinates are withheld.

spec.description: Unshaded circle with plain horizontal and vertical axes, a marked point P on the negative 120-degree ray in quadrant III, and an arrowhead beyond the circumference. The positive horizontal intercept is labelled 10.
spec.mathematics: Circle radius 10; −120° is coterminal with 240°, with reference angle 60°. P=(10 cos(−120°),10 sin(−120°)). Diagram coordinates are normalised by the radius.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied radius, angle and point label are visible; coordinates are withheld.

answer.worked:
$-120^{\circ}$ is coterminal with $240^{\circ}$, in quadrant III.
$$\begin{align*}x&=-10\cos60^{\circ}\\x&=-10\times\frac12\\x&=-5\\y&=-10\sin60^{\circ}\\y&=-10\times\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\y&=-5\sqrt3\\P&=(-5,-5\sqrt3)\end{align*}$$
